stage1.impression: A strong graphic idea: eight tinted cabinets in a spectrum lineup against board-formed concrete, doubled in a wet quay and a river. It still reads as CG. The washes are broad, low smudges with dark hill-shaped shadows between the speakers, not tall columns of light. The puddles are flat cut-out shapes with hard edges, a hairline seam runs down the wall into the third horn, the quay edge is a dead black band, and the denoiser has given the concrete and the cabinet edges a painterly smear. The product reads well and its colours sing, but there is no sense of a river front or of night air.

blocking_9: Each speaker throws a tall, distinct wash up the wall that blends with its neighbours, so the upper wall is clearly coloured above every horn instead of a grey-red murk (upper-wall luminance at least 1.5x the gaps between washes)
No dark hill-shaped shadow masses between the speakers at cabinet height
The wet quay reads as one continuous wet surface with soft-edged puddles, not flat decals with hard outlines
No formwork or panel seam running through a speaker or a horn
The quay edge reads as lit stone coping, not a crushed black band
Concrete and acrylic keep real micro-detail with no denoiser smear or posterised edges
Visible night atmosphere: a faint haze glow above each lamp and some depth beyond the quay

defects.what: Vertical hairline seam (a wall panel joint at x = -1.8) runs from the top of the frame straight into the Acid horn; edge step 16 levels
A second panel joint at x = +1.8 falls behind the Haze speaker
Dark hill-shaped shadow masses between the speakers at cabinet height; they read as smudges, not as light
The upper wall is a dull grey-red (median 41, R51 G38 B41). The washes do not rise tall or separate into eight colours
Puddles are flat, hard-edged cut-out shapes on dry-looking paving; they read as decals
The quay edge band is crushed black (61.6% crushed, median 2) with no stone detail
The river reflections are streaky and posterised, and there is nothing beyond them: no far bank, no depth
The denoiser gives the concrete a watercolour smear and posterises the cabinet edges and lining
The Smoke horn is a near-black void (median 10.7) with no edge separation from the wall
Eight identical copies with identical framing at uniform spacing: the setup is very graphic, and the repetition reads as an instanced model

changes.problem: The wall stands too far behind the speakers, so the 120 degree lamps light it broadly and the cabinets cast dark humps between them; the washes never rise tall or graze the board texture.

evidence.measured: between-speaker wall median 27 against a lit p95 of 140; upper-wall profile above the speakers runs 36-51 for its top half and rises only near the cabinets

changes.expected: Light from each lamp grazes up the wall in a tall, narrow column that rakes the board marks; the dark humps shrink to thin gaps; each wash is clearly its speaker's colour above its horn.

changes.problem: The washes are too weak to carry up a 5.6 m wall; the upper wall reads as moonlit grey, not coloured light.

out_of_scope.request: Give the Smoke black horn some edge separation from the wall
out_of_scope.why: The colour and material are fixed. Only the set's light (c1, c2) can help, by putting a brighter wash behind the horn so it reads in silhouette.

out_of_scope.request: Break the identical-copy feel by varying the cabinets
out_of_scope.why: The eight must be the same product. The variety has to come from the light and the wall, not from the speakers.

out_of_scope.request: Show the opera house's top edge, the sky or the far river bank to sell 'river front'
out_of_scope.why: This needs a wider, higher camera and changes the framing the shot's purpose fixes. It is worth a separate variant.
